newsitem.title: USA: US EPA says did record number enforcements in 1996.
newsitem.headline: US EPA says did record number enforcements in 1996.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said Tuesday it enforced a record high 557 civil and criminal cases last year, and assessed a total of $173 million in criminal, civil and administrative fines and penalties.
Of that, it said 262 criminal cases were referred to the Justice Department, and $76.7 million in criminal fines were assessed which was more than double the previous record.
The agency said polluters last year agreed to spend some $1.5 billion to correct violations, clean hazardous waste sites or take measures to prevent future problems.

Under EPA audit policies intended to encourage companies to voluntarily disclose and correct violations, last year 43 companies disclosed violations at 243 facilities and the EPA settled matters with 27 companies at 30 facilities.
